candidates.summary: Savings-gated pricing: the free tier converts to a paid plan only after verified savings reach 3x the price. The price is min($79, one third of verified monthly savings), and the plan stays free while the guarantee is not met.
candidates.hypothesis: Contradiction: 'AI CFO' tools cost $375-1,125/mo (cfo.ai), while founder finance tools cluster at $25-79 and banks bundle runway for free. Waste surveys claim 25-35% of SaaS spend is wasted, but in dollars a seed team's waste may only be ~$1-3K/mo, which is the gap that makes %-of-savings fail. Tying price to Runway's own verified-savings ledger (G1, already built) removes the WTP objection, but only if enough companies clear the bar. Predicted: at least 50% of synthetic companies with 15-35% planted waste reach 3x$79 of verified savings within 90 days of acting on findings, and under 20% of those with 0-5% planted waste do.
candidates.mve: Scratch script: generate 200+ companies (seeds x clean/noisy) and scale planted waste to 0/5/15/25/35% of SaaS spend (scratch wrapper that scales the truth items). Run detectFindings, simulate acceptance at a 60% act rate with a 0-2 month lag, advance asOf 90 days with post-cancel transactions removed, then run verifySavings. Report the share of companies clearing 3x$79 per waste level and the month-1 share of all savings (front-loading, which signals a retention cliff). Falsified if under 40% clear the bar at 25% waste, or if more than 80% of savings land in month 1 (the price would then rest on a one-time event).
evidence: research_notes/Runway product go to market/icp_pricing_distribution.md (sections 1-2: Cledara 25-35% waste, $49-149 band, Vertice guarantee, %-of-savings caveat)
research_notes/Runway product go to market/competitors.md (cfo.ai $375/$1,125 per month)

candidates.summary: A calibrated-trust Inbox. Every finding and draft shows a computed confidence score and an evidence receipt (transactions, cadence fit, price-change z-score). The Inbox ranks items by expected dollars x confidence and batches low-value items so they never reach the founder one by one.
candidates.hypothesis: Contradiction: vendors sell AI autonomy, and surveys disagree widely on trust: only 14% of CFOs trust AI accounting data (Esker/Techeconomy), while 56% of SMB finance leaders trust outputs 'completely or a lot' (BILL 2026). One reading is that trust tracks verifiability: people trust outputs they can check. If confidence scores are calibrated, ranking by expected value should let a fatigued approver who reviews only the top K items capture most of the planted dollars. This addresses G5 (approval fatigue) and G6 (generator overfitting).
candidates.mve: Scratch harness: perturb noisy generator feeds beyond the current eval (descriptor mangling, partial refunds, ±10% amount jitter, skipped months, a vendor renamed mid-stream) across 100 seeds. Derive a confidence score from existing detector internals and compute calibration (ECE, Brier) against planted truth plus negative controls. Simulate an approver who reviews only the top K = 3/5/10 items and compare captured planted dollars for EV-ranked versus current-order Inbox. Falsified if ECE > 0.10 or if the top 5 by EV capture under 80% of planted dollars.
evidence: sleep-research/IDEA_REPORT.md (G5, G6; Medius 90% require human approval)

candidates.summary: A blind-spot meter showing 'what your bank can't see'. From the Rho feed alone, detect autopay lump payments to other card issuers (Amex, Ramp, Brex, Chase) and estimate how much of the company's spend, and how much likely waste, sits off-feed. Then prompt the founder to drop in a card-statement CSV, which runs the same detectors on that spend.
candidates.hypothesis: Contradiction: banks and Ramp give waste insights away free, yet each covers only its own rails, and small teams don't buy SaaS-management tools ($10K+/yr, SSO-based). The free bank view therefore systematically under-reports waste for any multi-card startup. Predicted: when 30-50% of subscriptions move to an external card, single-feed recall of planted waste dollars falls below 60%, and (a) a lump-payment classifier flags the off-feed share within ±10 points while (b) a statement-CSV import restores recall to at least 95%. The size of that gap is a cross-bank acquisition hook that no bank is motivated to build (G2).
candidates.mve: Scratch fork of the generator: move a random 30/50% of subscriptions (including some planted waste) to a synthetic 'AMEX' card. The Rho feed then shows only a monthly 'AMEX EPAYMENT' lump, and a separate CSV holds the line items. Across 100 seeds, measure (1) dollar recall of planted waste on the Rho feed alone, (2) whether the lumps are classified as card payoffs and not double-counted in burn, (3) the off-feed share estimate versus truth, and (4) recall after a CSV merge using the existing normalize and detect pipeline. Falsified if single-feed recall stays at or above 80% (no blind spot worth selling) or if the CSV merge double-counts burn.
evidence: research_notes/Runway product go to market/competitors.md (sections 1 and 5: platforms see only their own rails; bank-agnostic wedge)
research_notes/Runway product go to market/competitors.md (section 2: SaaS mgmt minimums of ~$10K/yr)

candidates.summary: A backtested runway that matches the spreadsheet. The app imports the founder's plan (a CSV of monthly burn and revenue) and shows plan-vs-bank drift and the line items behind it. It also publishes a backtest of its own past runway calls for the account ('3 months ago we said 14.2, actual pace says 13.1'), with an 'investor haircut' range. A trend-aware forecast replaces the noise-only Monte Carlo band.
candidates.hypothesis: Contradiction: banks hand out runway for free, yet founders keep spreadsheets because a balance is not a forecast, and investors reportedly haircut founder projections by 30-50%. The README itself admits the MC band captures noise, not trends. A forecast that shows its own track record and reconciles to the founder's sheet should become the number a founder brings to the board, instead of a fourth spreadsheet. Predicted: on rolling-origin backtests, a trend-aware method (bootstrap plus a fitted burn and revenue drift) keeps P10-P90 coverage of realized 6-month-ahead cash at 70-90%. The current trailing-3-month and noise-only band falls below 60% whenever hiring or revenue trends are present.
candidates.mve: Scratch script: generate 100+ companies, adding in a scratch wrapper hiring step-ups (+$20-40K/mo), revenue ramps or declines (±5%/mo) and one-off shocks. For each rolling origin (months 9-18), forecast cash 3 and 6 months ahead with (a) computeSnapshot trailing runway, (b) the current forecastCash band and (c) a drift-adjusted variant. Score MAPE and P10-P90 coverage against realized cash. Separately, inject an optimistic 'plan' (revenue +20%, costs -15%, a missed hire) and test whether drift attribution names the right category in its top 3 at least 80% of the time. Falsified if the drift-adjusted variant does not beat (b) on coverage by 15+ points.
evidence: README.md (Known limitations: MC band captures noise not trends)
research_notes/Runway product go to market/competitors.md (Mercury Insights free runway)

candidates.summary: An exception-first portfolio triage board for fractional CFOs and accountants. Ranks 10-40 client companies by risk of breaching runway soon (P10 runway, burn acceleration, new alerts, unverified savings) and shows only exceptions. It is priced per client at a small fraction of the firm's retainer.
candidates.hypothesis: Contradiction: fractional CFOs bill $1.4K-15K per client per month, yet the bank-native monitoring they use is either free per single bank or a GL-based tool (Fathom, Jirav) that lags the books. No cheap multi-client, bank-feed tool exists (G3), and the firm channel is the faster path to ARR. Predicted: in a simulated 30-client portfolio, ranking by a composite risk score puts 80% or more of the clients that cross under 6 months of runway within the next 3 months into the top 5. A naive sort by current trailing runway catches 20+ points fewer of them, and the whole portfolio analyzes in under 1 second.
candidates.mve: Scratch script: build 50 portfolios of 30 synthetic companies each, from different seeds with randomized starting cash, burn scale, revenue trajectory and injected shocks (lost customer, hiring spree, annual renewals). At t0, score each client with (a) trailing runway and (b) a composite of P10 runway from forecastCash, burn slope, detectChanges severity and open waste. Measure recall@5 for clients that actually fall under 6 months of runway by t0+3 and the wall time per portfolio. Falsified if the composite's recall@5 lift over trailing runway is under 15 points.
evidence: research_notes/Runway product go to market/icp_pricing_distribution.md (Firm/Portfolio $20-40 per client; firm channel faster path to ARR)
